_about: Stage 5 script. One beat = one scene. vo is spoken (display spelling; brand pronunciations live in campaign.brand.say). voice.mode: recorded (you read the lines; the built-in files engine), clone (ref = a voice in voices/), design (pick a ref first), preset (name = an engine's stock voice) or none; voice.engine overrides campaign.voice_engine. spine: the question, stakes, turn, payoff and the loops (open questions, each opened and closed by a beat) that keep one question open from the hook to the payoff. Shape: hook by 2.5 s, first value by 6 s, re-hook half-way, payoff keeps the hook's promise (references/05-script.md). Variants replace beat B01 only, so hooks can be A/B tested on one body; `hook` is the one the video is made with (the pre-test winner), and only it is voiced and produced. spine.use is what the viewer does differently in their own life, in plain words; an apply beat (role apply, spoken to 'bạn'/'you') turns the book to the viewer before 80% of the runtime. recipe (mvflib/recipes.json) names what the script is built from; beats[].material cites the 00-material item ids each beat stands on (mvf material ls), the way facts cites F ids; beats[].art lists the approved generated pictures it shows (07-video/art/art.json, never the product UI or a real person). youtube is Shorts (9x16, ≤ 3 min); youtube-long is a 16x9 upload with its own scaffold and thumbnail. YouTube copy: title ≤ 70 chars with the search phrase first; the description's first line carries the search phrase, 1-3 #hashtags at the end; long-form chapters from 3 min (0:00 first, ≥ 3, each ≥ 10 s); thumbnail_text ≤ 5 words. Caption platforms (tiktok, instagram, facebook, linkedin): the promise and the search words in the first line, since the feed cuts the caption early; Instagram allows at most 5 #hashtags; LinkedIn autoplays muted, so its hook needs on-screen text. warn_notes answers a lint WARN that does not fit this script ({'V2': 'why'}); never bend the script to quiet one. Delete this _about when done.
value: what the viewer walks away with

spine.question: the one question the viewer stays to answer (opened by the hook)
spine.stakes: why it matters to this viewer: what is lost, won or wrong
spine.turn: what deepens or corrects the expected answer (optional; it never replaces the answer)
spine.payoff: the answer to the hook's question, in the form it asked (a verdict, a mapping, the cause, the steps)
spine.takeaway: the retell: the one or two sentences a stranger says after one viewing; the vo lines must say it
spine.use: answer: the answer they can now repeat, in the topic's words; lesson/decide/match/how-to: what they do or think differently in their own life, with no lore word

loops.q: the next, bigger question, opened before L1 closes

beats.visual: frame 0: the most interesting picture of the video, already moving (the result, the surprise); never a logo
first value by 6 s: the real product screen, its name in frame, pushed in on the control that matters
shots: the planned visible changes inside this beat (cut, push, reveal); the pacing check counts them

beats.visual: re-hook about half-way: the next, bigger thing
the viewer's own situation: what to do instead, spoken to 'you'
one soft line over the payoff picture: product name + handle, no logo card
